transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
In North Carolina, Democrat Chuck Hubbard has been elected to the U.S. House, defeating
11-term Republican Virginia Fox, according to a race call from the Associated Press.
It gives House Democrats their best general election results in decades, winning 258 seats
in an election sweep that hasn't been seen in more than 30 years.
The veteran Republican Congresswoman who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee conceded
today after a recount failed to close the narrow gap.
European Union negotiators are deeply disappointed with the collapse of climate talks in Turkey.
Terry Schultz reports the EU team says it couldn't accept the final draft that omitted
the mention of fossil fuel, considered one of the main drivers of environmental damage.
Despite record-long and extended negotiations to reach a compromise, Irish Environment Minister
Dara O'Brien, negotiating on behalf of the EU, said the absence of any mention of transitioning
away from coal, oil and gas was a disgrace.
We could not, with any good conscience, support a text that effectively denies what is happening
in the world and was hijacked by fossil fuel producers.
O'Brien's fellow negotiator, EU climate commissioner Wapke Hoekstra, echoed the disappointment.
This is larger than just all of us.
This is something that doesn't discriminate and that humanity urgently needs to tackle.
Hoekstra said the EU will continue working with like-minded countries and redouble its
own efforts to combat climate change.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
The suspected drone strike hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya today.
Libyan officials say the strike at the Benghazi naval base damaged the Mercury, a small Russian
warship, and started a fire at the base, and also say that the crew of the ship was rescued.
That ship was at the base for refueling and supplies as part of a Russian-Libyan agreement.
Starting January 1st, work requirements are being added to Medicaid, the public health
insurance program for low-income people.
Mayor Selena Simmons-Duffin reports health policy experts warn those new rules will increase
the number of people who are uninsured.
Right now, Medicaid covers about 70 million low-income Americans.
About 5 million of them are projected to become uninsured because of the new work requirements.
Adriana McIntyre is a health policy professor at Harvard.
She points out enrollment has to shrink in order to achieve savings in the Republican
budget law.
You can only save money in Medicaid if you're covering fewer people.
And if you're only covering fewer healthy people, you're not saving that much money.
It's covering fewer people who need health care.
That's where you get, scare quotes, savings out of work requirements.
Democrats say reversing this policy is a top priority when they take over the majority
in Congress.
Selena Simmons-Duffin reporting.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Justice Department told a court the U.S. Army intends to detonate nearly five tons of
toxic bomb-making material containing lead in Iowa this week despite a court order temporarily
halting it.
Critics say the blast could possibly contaminate hundreds of miles with toxic dust.
Lawyers for the Army say continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather
starts to turn colder.
At least three workers are dead, dozens are missing after a fire tore through a candy factory
west of Indonesia's capital.
The company says about 300 workers were inside when the fire broke out yesterday.
Nina Rao has the latest from Jakarta.
The fire started Saturday evening at the three-story facility west of Jakarta.
The factory produces milk-based candies and snacks.
Indonesia's search and rescue agency is still searching for more than two dozen missing workers
after evacuating 15 people on Sunday.
Some are being treated at a local hospital for injuries.
Responders are using water cannons to cool remaining hot spots amidst the building debris
as smoke continues billowing from the remaining embers and the collapsed structure.
Officials say the fires have been put out.
A cause has not been confirmed.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Rao in Jakarta, Indonesia.
At the weekend box office, the Hunger Games' "Sunrise on the Reaping" debuted in the top
spot with an estimated $120 million in ticket sales.
It focuses on the backstory of a beloved character, Hamish Abernathy.
This after 14 years and six movies is a sequel to "Songbirds and Snakes."
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins North Carolina House seat, defeating 11-term Republican Virginia Fox
EU negotiators express disappointment after climate talks collapse in Turkey over omitted fossil fuel language
Suspected drone strike damages Russian warship Mercury at Benghazi naval base in Libya
Medicaid work requirements take effect January 1, with about 5 million projected to lose coverage
Justice Department says Army plans to detonate nearly five tons of lead-containing bomb material in Iowa despite court order
Fire at a candy factory west of Jakarta, Indonesia kills at least three and leaves dozens missing
Hunger Games prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping" debuts at top of weekend box office with $120 million
